title: SQL LEFT JOIN: Why Your Missing Rows Disappear
scenes: Where did the other rows go?
We have three customers and two orders. One order is paid and the other is pending. We want every customer, along with any paid order they have. The example uses a small local database.

A left join keeps unmatched customers, but our filter runs after the join. It keeps only rows with a paid order. The pending order fails that test, and the missing order has no status at all. Both customers disappear.
Show rows before and after filtering.
Move the paid condition into the join itself. This changes which orders can match a customer. A customer without a matching paid order is still included, with missing order values.
Now all three customers appear. Only the first has a paid order. The other two have empty order values. We compare the actual rows against the expected result.

The two queries answer different questions. A filter after the join is useful when you only want customers with paid orders. Put the condition in the join when you want to preserve customers without a match.
notes: WHERE is applied after the join.
